Hi Chau, thanks for the patch. I've left some comments on the header for now, as I hope they can simplify the implementation.
Thanks for your review.
Do we need this in the public header? Again, my preference has become that we don't do this.
Disregard this, it was a comment without thought.
ACK
Table 77 PDR Type Values in DSP0248 v1.3.0 says this should be 30.
Done
'superior'? Also, please avoid contracting words like 'directory' to 'dir' arbitrarily, as it makes it harder to search the spec for the relevant member.
Done. Changed to `superior_directory_file_identifier`

`maximum` here, rather than `max`, as per the discussion above.

Please audit all the members for this concern.
Done
Rather use `struct variable_field` members for both.
Done. Please help review my edit.
See the suggestion above about `struct variable_field`. I hope we can avoid this dance.
Done
This shouldn't be `-EINVAL`? Maybe `-EBADMSG` (too short for fixed portion) or `-EOVERFLOW` (invalid variable-length portion).
Done. Updated to `-EOVERFLOW`
`-EOVERFLOW` as above.
Done
I think we can avoid this?
Done
We shouldn't need `file_name_len` here because we should use `struct variable_field`'s `length` member instead.
Done
As above.
Done

This is where we see more of the problem you hit here: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/libpldm/+/75364/comment/3bb868a5_e7e9a60c/

The length value should end up in `pdr->file_name.length` so the call on 3338 is correct.
Updated. Please help review.

Be wary of `pldm_msgbuf_span_string_ascii()` - it looks for a `NUL`-terminator in the message and should only be used if we don't know the length before-hand. DSP0248 does define this string as `NUL`-terminated, however, we've extracted the length above on line 3333, no scanning for a null-terminator is required in practice. Instead you can use `pldm_msgbuf_span_required()` here.
Done
See comment above regarding `file_name`.
Done
Hi Chau, I have a few more comments.
This isn't necessary, right? There's no-longer a flexible array member to cause `pdr` to vary in size.
Done
This shouldn't be necessary, see comment on header.
Done

We can just use a string here. It looks pretty noisy with the individual characters an then the numeric representation of `NUL`.

```
const char expectFileName[] = "File1";
```

Similarly throughout.
Done
The data for these tests is independent. Can you please split them into separate `TEST()` cases?
Done
